request.prompt:
You are extracting the numeric claims of one section of a model-validation report, so that each
can be checked against the artifact it cites. Section: monitoring.

List EVERY number that appears in the prose below, in the order it appears, including numbers that
appear inside a citation's logical name and numbers written with a thousands separator or a per
cent sign. For each one:

- "text" is the whole line the number appears on, copied exactly, citations included.
- "value" is the number as written, with thousands separators and the per cent sign removed:
  "3,500" is 3500, "22.0%" is 22.0.
- "unit" is "percent" when the number is written with a per cent sign, "count" for a number of
  rows, features or events, "currency", "bp" for basis points, "months" for a horizon, and
  "ratio" for every other dimensionless quantity (AUC, PSI, VIF, a coefficient, a lift).
- "metric" is what the number measures, taken from the logical name of the artifact it cites
  (auc, brier, psi, vif, calibration_slope, delta_auc, coefficient, event_rate, ...), or null.
- "split" is train, test, out_of_time or vintage_holdout, or null.
- "comparison" is "eq" for a number that equals its artifact; "delta" for a difference written
  "from a to b" or "a gap of x", whose value is the second cited artifact minus the first; and
  "ratio" for a number written as one artifact divided by another. A delta or ratio carries TWO
  adjacent citations, in that order.
- "citation" is the [[art:...]] token the number carries, copied exactly, or null when the
  sentence carries none. Do not invent a citation and do not move one from another number.
- "rounding" is the number of decimals the prose wrote when it wrote fewer than the artifact has
  (2 for a lift written 2.24), or null.

Return every number even when it has no citation: a number you leave out is still counted, and
counted against the report.

Prose:
Ongoing monitoring should evaluate the extent to which this model continues to perform as expected given potential changes in products, exposures, activities, clients, data relevance, or market conditions, and should route any deterioration into overlays, adjustment, or redevelopment under the owning organization's model risk policy [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].

The frequency and scope of the monitoring reports recommended below should be set by the nature of this model, the availability of new data, and its materiality in use, and should be revisited when any of those change [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].

### Quantities to track and the bound to track them against

Monitoring should re-use the threshold artifacts this validation exercised rather than introduce fresh bounds, so that a monitoring breach and a validation failure mean the same thing.

- Discrimination: track AUC on each newly scored and outcome-matured cohort against the declared minimum of 0.7 [[art:8bfd02cc:threshold.package.auc.test.min]], reading the validated test value of 0.755 [[art:365b7034:metrics.test.auc]] as the baseline from which drift is measured.
- Calibration slope: track the logistic regression of the outcome on logit(p) against the declared band, whose lower edge is 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] and whose upper edge is 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]], with the validated value of 0.9886 [[art:e06564c7:calibration_slope.test]] as the baseline.
- Probability accuracy: track the Brier score against the declared maximum of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]].
- Population and score stability: track the largest PSI across input features and the score itself against the declared maximum of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]], with the validated train-to-test value of 0.003083 [[art:e1d82330:psi.max]] as the baseline.
- Runtime: track the scoring job's wall-clock time against the declared cap of 300.0 [[art:3f4c6e97:threshold.package.max_seconds]] seconds, since a cap breach is an implementation signal even when the metrics hold.
- Reporting order: when the realized event rate in a monitoring cohort falls below 0.05 [[art:42f1351e:rule.calibration_first_event_rate]], the monitoring report should present calibration before discrimination, matching the ordering rule this report followed.

### Frequency

Stability and runtime quantities do not wait on outcomes and should be computed on every scoring run, with the PSI and wall-clock figures carried into a monthly summary.

Discrimination, calibration slope, and Brier score depend on realized defaults and should therefore be reported on a cycle no shorter than the outcome maturation window for this portfolio, which in practice means a quarterly report on the most recently matured cohort.

The full set should also be recomputed out of cycle on any change to the upstream feeds, the feature definitions, or the scoring code, because none of the baselines above survive such a change unexamined.

A breach of any declared bound, or a sustained one-sided drift within a bound, should trigger investigation before the next scheduled report rather than at it.

### What this validation could not cover

This validation was performed on a single train-and-test split, so it says nothing about performance across an economic cycle, and monitoring is the only place where out-of-time deterioration will become visible.

This validation did not observe the model in a production system, so process verification of the deployed pipeline, including input completeness, feature-definition drift, and change control over the scoring code, has to be carried by monitoring [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].

This validation did not analyze overrides, since none exist before use, and monitoring should log every case where model output is ignored, altered, or reversed, evaluate the reasons, and track whether the override process consistently improves on the model [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].

This validation did not benchmark the model against an alternative internal model or against retail credit bureau data, and monitoring should establish such a comparison and investigate the source and degree of any discrepancy rather than treat agreement as reassurance [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].

This validation did not test performance within subpopulations or at the edges of the input ranges the model was fit on, so monitoring should report the declared metrics by segment and flag cohorts that approach or leave those ranges.

Material model risk can remain even where modeling and validation were sound, so users of this model's output should continue to communicate its limitations and supplement the score with complementary analysis rather than rely on the monitoring bounds alone [[reg:SR26-2:V]].
